title: Regular expressions
description: Regex is the fastest path through string-parsing interview problems — know the literals, flags, capture groups, and the difference between `replace` and `replaceAll`.

notes: `String.prototype.replace` with a plain string replaces only the FIRST occurrence — use `/g` or `.replaceAll`.
Inside a `new RegExp('...')` string, you must double-escape — `'\\d+'` matches one digit-class.
`'abc'.match(/x/)` returns `null` (not `[]`) when there is no match — guard before indexing.

questions.q: Which flag makes a regex match all occurrences in `.match` / `.replace`?
What does `'a-b'.replace('-', '_')` return when the input is `'a-b-c'`?
questions.explain: String-arg replace only swaps the first occurrence.

questions.q: How do you reference the second capture group in a replacement string?
What does `'abc'.match(/x/)` return when there is no match?
questions.explain: Guard for null before indexing into the result.

exercises.prompt: Extract every run of digits from the string.
Swap first and last names using a capture group.

L3.prompt: Write `slugify(s)` that lowercases the string, replaces every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single `-`, and trims leading/trailing `-`. Log `slugify('  Hello, World!! ')`.
hints: Use `[^a-z0-9]+` with the `g` flag to collapse runs.
